question: Can a precommitted four-coordinate signed-digit Hensel rule reach the same p-adic residual depth with smaller exact rational model height than the first-axis rule?
public_hit: copy the first eligible distinct-x public hit from the baseline result; do not reselect
digit_rule: at depth k, evaluate t(R) modulo p^(k+1) and the four finite differences from +p^k coordinate probes; if t already vanishes retain shifts; otherwise find signed digits delta_i in [-(p-1)/2,(p-1)/2] satisfying sum_i d_i*delta_i = -t/p^k (mod p), minimizing (max_i abs(delta_i), sum_i abs(delta_i), signed digit tuple lexicographically)
digit_solver: meet-in-the-middle pair sums; enumerate radii h=0,1,..., and record the complete minimum-radius candidate count and tie score; independently verify no smaller or better digit tuple
coordinate_update: shift_i += p^(k-1)*delta_i, so lifted coordinate_i += p^k*delta_i
exact_controls: after each accepted step compute exact rational A,B,P1,P2,R and t=-x(R)/y(R), check curve/reduction and depth; independently replay every derivative and digit choice with Fraction group arithmetic
comparison: paired same public hit, same starting rational model, same target depth, same checked Sage runtime; report per-depth model and residual heights for both paths; time is diagnostic only
stop_rule: stop at exact relation, derivative exhaustion, modular or exact mismatch, depth 8, or 1200 seconds; preserve failed probes
claim_boundary: this is a representation-height comparison for one preselected public relation, not an estimate of natural relation yield or an end-to-end IC/rho comparison
